notes: Two moves-against-the-bank records cross-filed from corruption cases already on the map, found by grepping writeups.json for the absent list rather than by any new research. No new sources were opened: both rest on the source already cited by the country's own corruption case. PNG reverses a round-44 exclusion on the reasoning, and the reversal is written into cross_layer.py rather than made quietly. Tonga and Bosnia and Herzegovina were examined on the same pass and both stay excluded, with their reasons recorded.

records.summary: Court documents obtained by the journalism group OCCRP show that Papua New Guinea's National Fraud and Anti-Corruption Directorate searched the offices of the Bank of Papua New Guinea in August and September 2023, as part of a money-laundering investigation in which the bank's then acting governor, Elizabeth Genia, was the subject. She obtained a temporary stay of the investigation which was later dismissed, and she was appointed governor in early 2024. She has not been charged and nothing in the investigation is proven. What is recorded here is the act of the state: a national law-enforcement directorate entering and searching the central bank's own premises, which is the same shape as the Slovenian police search of Banka Slovenije already on this layer.
records.source_title: PNG Central Bank Chief Appointed Amid Money Laundering Investigation (OCCRP)

records.summary: A report of the Office of the Ombudsman of Vanuatu dated 3 July 1996 found that the governor of the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu, Samson Ngwele, improperly executed ten bank guarantees totalling 100 million US dollars without the approval of the bank's board and under pressure from the Minister of Finance, Barak Sope, in breach of the Reserve Bank Act and the Leadership Code. The guarantees were issued to Peter Harold Swanson for a trading programme the Ombudsman described as a scam, and were still in circulation when the report was written. No governor was removed: what the record describes is a minister pressing the governor into committing the bank, found by the state's own Ombudsman, with the corruption findings against the governor staying in the corruption case.
records.source_title: The Provision of Bank Guarantees Given in the Sum of US$100,000,000.00 (Office of the Ombudsman, Vanuatu, via PacLII)
